title: Rate Guard telemetry and graceful degradation playbook for quota-control outages
creator: Aisha Patel
description: The platform's quota-control layer can become a single point of user-visible disruption during partial outages (network partitions, redis lease failures, or quota-store lag). This ticket designs and implements 'Rate Guard' — a telemetry-driven graceful degradation system and operator playbook that ensures SLO-aligned behavior during limiter outages: (1) detect degraded quota enforcement via synthesized health signals, (2) apply SLO-first shedding policies across regions, (3) open short-lived circuit breakers with progressive re-admission, and (4) provide clear runbook actions to restore correctness. Goal: minimize 99th latency and overall error-rate regressions while preserving fairness across tenants during emergency modes.
acceptance_criteria: automatic detection: anomaly rule detects quota-store lease loss within 30s with <=1m false positive rate
degradation policy: system can switch to SLO-first shedding policy and reduce 99th latency violations by >=40% under simulated quota controller outage
fairness: weighted soft-eviction preserves proportional share for top-100 tenants in replay test within 10% of baseline throughput distribution
circuit breaker: progressive re-admit flows restore full capacity with no more than 3% error spike on rejoin in canary region
observability: dashboard shows signal footprint (rate_guard.state, affected_tenants, shed_fraction) and alerts escalate to oncall when customer_impact is high
design_decisions: telemetry-first: use a composite health signal (redis leases, token-bucket drift, request-latency slope) rather than a single boolean to avoid oscillation
slo-prioritized shedding: drop lower-SLO routes before others; implement per-tenant weight decay rather than hard cutoffs to maintain degraded fairness
regional autonomy: allow regional controllers to independently enter Rate Guard mode but publish a compact state summary to global control plane for cross-region coordination
short-lived circuit breakers: breakers open for exponential backoff windows with tokenized re-admission to avoid thundering herd on recovery
operator playbook: combine automated mitigations with explicit manual steps (traffic reroute, quota-store failover, emergency cache clear) to balance automation and control
implementation_steps: 1) add composite health metric stream (rate_guard.lease_ok, rate_guard.kv_lag_ms, rate_guard.token_drift_pct) and wire into metrics pipeline
2) implement SLO-first shedding policy module in rate-controller with soft-eviction weighting and tenant-preserving heuristics
3) add circuit breaker layer with progressive re-admit: tokenized slots + exponential backoff
4) expose control endpoints for operator interventions (force-enter, force-exit, set-shed-threshold, tenant-exclude)
5) create dashboards and alert rules; add runbook to ops playbooks with step-by-step recovery
6) unit/integration tests, chaos simulation harness for network partition and lease flapping scenarios
7) staged rollout: internal canary -> region canary -> global rollout with telemetry gates
testing_plan: synthetic chaos tests simulating redis lease loss and topology partition across 3 regions
replay of production traffic for top-1k tenants under degraded mode to validate fairness heuristics
bench tests measuring 99th latency and token cost with and without Rate Guard enabled
fuzz tests for breaker re-admit sequences to ensure no deadlock or stampede
manual run of operator playbook in staging with oncall present
monitoring_and_alerting: dashboard: rate_guard.overview (state by region, affected_routes, shed_fraction, tenant_histogram)
alerts: P1 if rate_guard.state == 'degraded' for >2 minutes and affected_tenants > 5
alerts: P0 if shed_fraction > 50% or SLO breach rate rises > 5% above baseline
logging: structured reason codes emitted for every shed decision to allow postmortem reconstruction
tracing: attach shed_reason tag to sampled requests for latency/error correlation
rollout_and_rollback: phase 0: unit/integration tests pass in CI and chaos harness metrics look stable
phase 1: internal canary behind feature flag in us-central1 with 5% traffic for 48h
phase 2: regional canaries (eu-west1, ap-southeast1) incremental 5% -> 25% with safety gates
phase 3: global rollout with traffic ramp + monitor SLO gates for 24h per region
rollback: immediate feature-flag disable if P0 alert fires or shed_fraction > 60%
post-deploy: 72h observation window and 1-week postmortem if any SLO regression
